'''Leo Kouwenhoven''' (born {{Birth date|1963|12|10|df=yes}}) is a Dutch [[List of physicists|physicist]] known for his research on [[quantum computing]], specifically in [[Topological quantum computer|topological quantum computing]] experiments.

== Education ==
Kouwenhoven grew up in [[Pijnacker]], a village near [[Delft]], where his parents ran a farm. After losing the [[University and college admission|admission lottery]] for [[veterinary medicine]] he decided to study [[physics]] at [[Delft University of Technology]] (TU Delft).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Hoeks|first=Louis|date=2016-03-06|title='Op de boerderij leerde ik dat wegduiken geen optie is'|url=https://fd.nl/profiel/1141978/op-de-boerderij-leerde-ik-dat-wegduiken-geen-optie-is|publisher=Financieele Dagblad}}</ref>

In 1992 he received his PhD ''[[Latin honors|cum laude]]'' at TU Delft; his promoter was {{Interlanguage link|Hans Mooij|de}}. 

== Career ==
In 1999 he became a [[professor]] at TU Delft.<ref name=":0" /> In 2007 he received the [[Spinoza Prize]], the highest Dutch academic award. In April 2012 his TU Delft research group presented experimental results that provided potential "signatures" of [[Majorana fermion]] [[quasiparticle]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2012-04-evidence-majorana-fermions.html |title=Researchers find possible evidence of Majorana fermions |author=Bob Yirka |work=phys.org |date=2012-04-13 |access-date=2024-05-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.engineersonline.nl/nanowetenschappers-vinden-langgezocht-majorana-deeltje-video/ |title=Nanowetenschappers vinden langgezocht Majorana-deeltje |work=engineersonline.nl |date= 17 February 1999|language=nl |access-date=2024-05-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mourik|first1=V.|last2=Zuo|first2=K.|last3=Frolov|first3=S. M.|last4=Plissard|first4=S. R.|last5=Bakkers|first5=E. P. a. M.|last6=Kouwenhoven|first6=L. P.|date=2012-05-25|title=Signatures of Majorana Fermions in Hybrid Superconductor-Semiconductor Nanowire Devices|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1222360|journal=Science|language=en|volume=336|issue=6084|pages=1003–1007|doi=10.1126/science.1222360|issn=0036-8075|pmid=22499805|arxiv=1204.2792|bibcode=2012Sci...336.1003M |s2cid=18447180}}</ref> These Majorana quasiparticles would be very stable, and therefore suitable for building a quantum computer.<ref>Robert F. Service, [http://news.sciencemag.org/sciencenow/2012/04/majorana-fermions-found.html Physicists Discover New Type of Particle — Sort Of], ''ScienceNOW'', 12 April 2012</ref>

In 2018 his research group claimed to have proved the definitive existence of Majorana particles in a ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' publication.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Hao|last2=Liu|first2=Chun-Xiao|last3=Gazibegovic|first3=Sasa|last4=Xu|first4=Di|last5=Logan|first5=John A.|last6=Wang|first6=Guanzhong|last7=van Loo|first7=Nick|last8=Bommer|first8=Jouri D. S.|last9=de Moor|first9=Michiel W. A.|last10=Car|first10=Diana|last11=Op het Veld|first11=Roy L. M.|date=2018|title=RETRACTED ARTICLE: Quantized Majorana conductance|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature26142|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=556|issue=7699|pages=74–79|doi=10.1038/nature26142|pmid=29590094|issn=1476-4687|arxiv=1710.10701|s2cid=4613547}}{{Retracted|doi=10.1038/s41586-021-03373-x|pmid=33686283|http://retractionwatch.com/2021/03/08/authors-retract-nature-majorana-paper-apologize-for-insufficient-scientific-rigour/ ''Retraction Watch''|intentional=yes}}</ref> However, the results could not be reproduced by other scientists, and the article had to be retracted in 2021 due to "insufficient scientific rigour".<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1038/s41586-021-03373-x|title = Retraction Note: Quantized Majorana conductance|year = 2021|last1 = Zhang|first1 = Hao|last2 = Liu|first2 = Chun-Xiao|last3 = Gazibegovic|first3 = Sasa|last4 = Xu|first4 = Di|last5 = Logan|first5 = John A.|last6 = Wang|first6 = Guanzhong|last7 = Van Loo|first7 = Nick|last8 = Bommer|first8 = Jouri D. <ref>{{Cite web|title=Landmark article by QuTech researchers under scrutiny|url=https://www.delta.tudelft.nl/article/landmark-article-qutech-researchers-under-scrutiny|access-date=2021-03-08|website=Landmark article by QuTech researchers under scrutiny {{!}} TU Delta|date=19 May 2020 |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Stan van Pelt|date=2021-02-23|title=Hoe jonge onderzoekers het fundament wegsloegen onder de quantumdroom van een Delftse hoogleraar|url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/gs-b38f971b|access-date=2021-03-08|website=de Volkskrant|language=nl-NL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Nature paper 'Quantized Majorana conductance', report from independent experts|url=https://zenodo.org/record/4545812|website=Zenodo|year=2021|doi=10.5281/zenodo.4545812|language=en|last1=Brouwer|first1=Piet|last2=Ensslin|first2=Klaus|last3=Goldhaber-Gordon|first3=David|last4=Lee|first4=Patrick|s2cid=244959752 }}</ref> The researchers had excluded data points that contradicted their claims, with the complete data not supporting their conclusions.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/microsoft-win-quantum-computing-error/|title=Microsoft's Big Win in Quantum Computing Was an 'Error' After All|magazine=Wired}}</ref>

Two of the Majorana research papers involving Leo Kouwenhoven's group at QuTech were retracted due to data irregularities, leading to a couple of investigations by the TU Delft's Research Integrity Committee (CWI) and the Dutch Body for Scientific Integrity (LOWI) between 2020 and 2023.{{Efn|CWI and the LOWI led a first investigation between 2020 and 2022. The CWI conducted a second investigation from 2022 to 2023}} While Kouwenhoven was found partly negligent in one case, no scientific integrity violations were confirmed.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Timeline retracted Majorana papers |url=https://qutech.nl/research-engineering/qubit-research/retracted-majorana-papers/ |access-date=2024-10-23 |website=QuTech |language=en-US}}</ref>

Kouwenhoven was reappointed as university professor at TU Delft in 2024.<ref name=":1" />

== Personal life ==
Kouwenhoven has six sisters and is married to [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] professor Marleen Huysman.<ref name=":0" />
